subtitles.en: You and your colleagues have done this survey of consumers who are going to maybe avail themselves of these discounts and you look at spending during Prime Day. That's one of the questions that you ask. How much consumers intend to spend when these Prime Day celebrations are underway?
subtitles.zh: 你和同事做了这项调查，了解消费者在Prime Day期间的消费意愿。你们问的一个问题是，消费者计划花多少钱？

subtitles.en: And I'm curious what those numbers tell you. Maybe we have a screenshot that we can put on the screen. It seems like it's mostly in the middle there between $101 and $200. So not an extremely large amount of money that people plan to spend.
subtitles.zh: 这些数字说明了什么？屏幕上显示，大部分计划消费在101到200美元之间，金额并不大。

subtitles.en: What does it tell you about the health of the consumer more broadly? They're appetite to spend more. They're capacity to spend more right now and we see kind of the economic constraints at play that we do.
subtitles.zh: 这反映了消费者的整体状况？他们的消费意愿和能力受到经济限制的影响。

subtitles.en: Yeah, so consumers are definitely pulling back, which is what makes this day important. As you mentioned, you know, when you look at the sweet spotter that mid-range here, between $100, $200, it's about the same really as last year.
subtitles.zh: 消费者确实在缩减开支，这让Prime Day变得重要。中间价位100到200美元与去年持平。

subtitles.en: But when you look at the higher band here at the $500 or above, you can see that there's a slight pullback. So there is some pullback that we are expecting this year based on higher gas prices, just inflation from tariffs, etc.
subtitles.zh: 但在500美元以上的高端区间，我们看到略有回落。由于油价上涨和关税带来的通胀，我们预计今年会有回落。

subtitles.en: And we do think that consumers are going to be deal savvy. In fact, you know, in our survey, we had asked how many of you have a list before going into Prime Day and what you want to buy? And it was over 50% said that they have a list of what they intend to buy on Prime Day.
subtitles.zh: 我们认为消费者会精打细算。调查中，超过50%的人表示在Prime Day前会列好购物清单。

subtitles.en: And not only that when we look at the categories that they're buying on Prime Day, it's not your big ticket items. I mean, it is, but it isn't all of it. There's a lot of everyday items that they're planning to buy.
subtitles.zh: 而且他们购买的商品类别并非大件商品，而是很多日常用品。

subtitles.en: And that just kind of goes to show you that Prime Day is important because they're looking to buy what they wanted for maybe last three months or into the next three months on Prime Day to really take advantage of those deep deals.
subtitles.zh: 这表明Prime Day很重要，因为他们想利用深度折扣购买过去或未来三个月需要的商品。

subtitles.en: You also found in your research that agentic sales are increasing to $500 billion by 2030. And I turned you our producer this morning, Patrick. And I said, what does that mean? Does that mean like AI is procuring things for companies?
subtitles.zh: 你的研究还发现，到2030年，代理式销售将增至5000亿美元。这是否意味着AI为企业采购？

subtitles.en: And he said, no, that can include a lot of things. So can you explain to us what you mean in a retail setting by agentic sales and agentic agents? And why this is going to be such a big thing? And it already is becoming such a big thing so quickly.

subtitles.en: Absolutely. So when you think about e-commerce sales today, most of them happen through your mobile app, you browsing and buying them directly. Agentic has a few different ways. You could look at it. One is fully agentic and one is semi-agentic.
subtitles.zh: 当然。如今电商销售大多通过手机应用直接浏览购买。代理式有几种方式：完全代理和半代理。

subtitles.en: So the $500 billion number that you refer to is fully agentic. That means you go into an agent and you say, I'd like to buy a black dress for Prime. Let's just say that's your query. That's all you have to say.
subtitles.zh: 你提到的5000亿美元是指完全代理。你只需对代理说，我想买一条黑色连衣裙，仅此而已。

subtitles.en: One prompt and it knows where you want to buy it. It knows how much you want to spend and it knows how soon you need it and it just ships to your door. Now, is that going to happen for that black dress for Prime? Probably not.
subtitles.zh: 一个指令，它就知道在哪里买、花多少钱、多快送到，然后直接发货。但黑色连衣裙可能不会这样。

subtitles.en: But will it happen for your laundry detergent, for your gallon of milk, for your tools, for your tires? Sure. So replenishment items are a big part of the fully agentic equation, but semi-agentic, which is when you use an AI agent to talk back and forth to like Amazon Alexa for shopping.
subtitles.zh: 但洗衣液、牛奶、工具、轮胎呢？当然。补充型商品是完全代理的重要部分，而半代理则是与Alexa等AI代理对话购物。

subtitles.en: It's when you engage the agent to search for something. For example, when you use Alexa for shopping, you go ahead and say, I want this power washer, for example, and find me the best power washer and needs to wash this many square feet and needs to have AI abilities, et cetera.
subtitles.zh: 半代理是让代理搜索商品。比如用Alexa购物，你说我想要高压清洗机，找到最好的，能清洗这么多平方英尺，具备AI功能等。

subtitles.en: And it needs to be under $500. Today, it's $650. When it drops to 500, I should have it. And it just happened in three weeks when it drops, you'll have it at your door.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
